names: Wife of Liu Min's younger brother

units.zh: 張介福 倪瓚 徐舫 楊恆 陳洄 楊引 吳海 劉閔 楊黼 孫一元 沈周 陳繼儒
units.en: Zhang Jiefu, Ni Zan, Xu Fang, Yang Heng, Chen Hui, Yang Yin, Wu Hai, Liu Min, Yang Fu, Sun Yiyuan, Shen Zhou, and Chen Jiru
units.literal: Zhang Jiefu, Ni Zan, Xu Fang, Yang Heng, Chen Hui, Yang Yin, Wu Hai, Liu Min, Yang Fu, Sun Yiyuan, Shen Zhou, Chen Jiru

units.zh: 韓愈言：「《蹇》之六二曰『王臣蹇蹇』，而《蠱》之上九曰『高尚其事』，由所居之時不一，而所蹈之德不同。」
units.en: Han Yu wrote: "The second line of the Hexagram Jian reads, 'The king's ministers are in distress,' while the top line of Gu reads, 'Noble in his deeds'—for the age each man lived in was not the same, and the virtue each man embodied was not the same."
units.literal: Han Yu said: "In the second line of Jian it says 'the king's ministers are in distress,' while in the top line of Gu it says 'noble in his conduct'—because the times in which they lived were not the same, the virtues they practiced were different."

units.zh: 夫聖賢以用世為心，而逸民以肥遁為節 ，豈性分實然，亦各行其志而已。
units.en: Sages and worthies set their hearts on serving the world, while men of retirement take luxuriant withdrawal as their standard of conduct. Was their nature utterly different? Each simply followed his own resolve.
units.literal: Sages and worthies take serving the age as their heart, while recluses take prosperous withdrawal as their integrity—is it that their natures are utterly different? Each merely followed his own aspiration.

units.zh: 明太祖興禮儒士，聘文學，搜求岩穴，側席幽人，後置不為君用之罰，然韜跡自遠者，亦不乏人。
units.en: When the Hongwu Emperor revived ritual and honored Confucian scholars, he recruited men of letters, sought out hermits in mountain caves, and waited eagerly for recluses to appear. Later he imposed penalties on those who refused to serve the throne, yet men who hid their tracks and kept their distance were never in short supply.
units.literal: Taizu of Ming promoted ritual and Confucian scholars, recruited men of letters, searched out those in mountain caves, and waited anxiously for recluses; later he imposed penalties on those who would not serve the ruler—yet those who hid their traces and kept far away were not lacking.

units.zh: 迨中葉承平，聲教淪浹，巍科顯爵，頓天網以羅英俊，民之秀者，無不觀國光而賓王廷矣。
units.en: By the mid-dynasty, in an age of peace, civilization had spread to every corner. Grand examinations and high offices cast the great net to gather the gifted, and none of the finest men among the people failed to behold the nation's splendor and present themselves at the royal court.
units.literal: When the middle period enjoyed peace, culture penetrated everywhere; eminent degrees and lofty ranks cast the great net to gather the talented—none of the outstanding among the people failed to behold the nation's glory and present themselves at the royal court.

units.zh: 其抱瑰材，蘊積學，槁形泉石，絕意當世者，靡得而稱焉。
units.en: Those who held rare gifts, hoarded learning, wasted their bodies among springs and stones, and turned their backs on the world could scarcely be named at all.
units.literal: Those who embraced rare talent, stored up learning, withered their forms among springs and rocks, and cut off all concern for the age—there was scarcely any way to name them.

units.zh: 由是觀之，世道升降之端，系所遭逢，豈非其時為之哉。
units.en: Seen in this light, whether the age rises or falls turns on what fortune brings—was it not the times that shaped it?
units.literal: Viewed thus, the turning points in the rise and fall of the world depend on what one encounters—is it not the times that make it so?

units.zh: 凡徵聘所及，文學行誼可稱者，已散見諸傳。
units.en: All those reached by summons and appointment whose learning and conduct were worthy of note have already appeared in scattered biographies elsewhere.
units.literal: All those reached by summons and recruitment whose literary accomplishment and conduct were praiseworthy have already been scattered through various biographies.

units.zh: 茲取貞節超邁者數人，作《隱逸傳》。
units.en: Here several men of steadfast integrity and extraordinary character are gathered to form the "Biographies of Recluses."
units.literal: Here several persons of steadfast integrity and transcendent character are selected to compose the "Biographies of Recluses."

units.zh: 張介福
units.en: Zhang Jiefu
units.literal: Zhang Jiefu

units.zh: 張介福，字子祺，自懷慶徙吳中。
units.en: Zhang Jiefu, courtesy name Ziqi, moved from Huaiqing to the Wu region.
units.literal: Zhang Jiefu, styled Ziqi, moved from Huaiqing to Wu.

units.zh: 少受學於許衡。
units.en: As a youth he studied under Xu Heng.
units.literal: In youth he studied under Xu Heng.

units.zh: 二親早終，遂無仕進意。
units.en: Both his parents died while he was young, and he lost all desire to pursue an official career.
units.literal: Both parents died early, and he thus had no intention of entering office.

units.zh: 家貧，冬不能具夾襦，或遺以𦆭絮，不受，纖介必以禮。
units.en: His family was poor, and in winter he could not afford a lined coat. When someone sent him cotton wadding for warmth, he refused it. Even the smallest courtesy had to be observed with strict propriety.
units.literal: His family was poor; in winter he could not afford lined robes. When someone sent him cotton padding, he would not accept it. Even the smallest matter had to observe ritual propriety.

units.zh: 張士誠入吳，有卒犯其家，危坐不為起。
units.en: When Zhang Shicheng entered Wu, a soldier broke into his home, but Jiefu sat upright and would not rise.
units.literal: When Zhang Shicheng entered Wu, a soldier violated his household; he sat upright and did not rise.

units.zh: 刀斫面，僕地，醒復取冠戴之，坐自若。
units.en: A blade struck his face and he fell to the ground. When he came to, he put his cap back on and resumed his seat as if nothing had happened.
units.literal: A blade hacked his face; he fell to the ground. When he woke he put his cap back on and sat as before.

units.zh: 卒怪，以為異物，走去。
units.en: The soldier was unnerved, took him for something uncanny, and fled.
units.literal: The soldier thought it strange, took him for something uncanny, and fled.

units.zh: 介福恐發其先墓，往廬焉。
units.en: Jiefu feared his ancestors' graves would be disturbed and went to live in a hut beside them.
units.literal: Jiefu feared his ancestors' tombs would be disturbed and went to live in a mourning hut beside them.

units.zh: 士誠聞而欲致之，不可。
units.en: Shicheng heard of him and wished to bring him into service, but could not.
units.literal: Shicheng heard of this and wished to summon him, but could not succeed.

units.zh: 使其弟往問，答曰：「無樂亂，無貪天禍，無忘國家。」
units.en: He sent his younger brother to inquire after him. Jiefu answered: "Take no joy in rebellion, covet no disaster sent by Heaven, and do not forget the nation."
units.literal: He sent his younger brother to inquire. Jiefu replied: "Do not take pleasure in disorder; do not covet Heaven's calamity; do not forget the state."

units.zh: 饋之，力辭。
units.en: When gifts were sent to him, he firmly refused them.
units.literal: When gifts were sent to him, he firmly declined.

units.zh: 已，病革，謂其友曰：「吾志希古人，未能也。
units.en: Later, when his illness grew critical, he told his friends: "My aspiration was to emulate the ancients, but I have not achieved it.
units.literal: Later, when his illness grew critical, he told his friends: "My aspiration was to emulate the ancients, but I have not achieved it.

units.zh: 惟無污於時，庶幾哉。」
units.en: Only that I have not been stained by my age—perhaps that much."
units.literal: Only that I have not been stained by the age—perhaps that much."

units.zh: 遂卒。
units.en: With that he died.
units.literal: Then he died.

units.zh: 倪瓚，字元鎮，無錫人也。
units.en: Ni Zan, courtesy name Yuanzhen, was a native of Wuxi.
units.literal: Ni Zan, styled Yuanzhen, was a man of Wuxi.

units.zh: 家雄於貲，工詩，善書畫。
units.en: His family was immensely wealthy. He was accomplished in poetry and excelled at calligraphy and painting.
units.literal: His family was wealthy; he was skilled in poetry and excelled at calligraphy and painting.

units.zh: 四方名士日至其門。
units.en: Renowned men of letters from every quarter came to his door each day.
units.literal: Famous scholars from all quarters came daily to his door.

units.zh: 所居有閣曰清閟，幽迥絕塵。
units.en: His residence held a pavilion called Qingbi, secluded and utterly removed from the dust of the world.
units.literal: In his residence was a pavilion called Qingbi, secluded and far removed from the dust of the world.

units.zh: 藏書數千卷，皆手自勘定。
units.en: He kept several thousand volumes in his library, every one collated by his own hand.
units.literal: He kept several thousand volumes of books, all collated by his own hand.

units.zh: 古鼎法書，名琴奇畫，陳列左右。
units.en: Ancient bronzes, masterworks of calligraphy, famous zithers, and extraordinary paintings were arrayed all around him.
units.literal: Ancient tripods, model calligraphy, famous zithers, and rare paintings were displayed on either side.

units.zh: 四時卉木，縈繞其外，高木修篁，蔚然深秀，故自號雲林居士。
units.en: Flowers and trees of every season encircled the pavilion outside, and tall timber and slender bamboo rose in lush, deep beauty. He therefore styled himself the Recluse of Cloud Forest.
units.literal: Flowers and trees of the four seasons encircled it outside; tall trees and tall bamboo stood lush and deep in beauty, and so he styled himself the Recluse of Cloud Forest.

units.zh: 時與客觴詠其中。
units.en: He would often drink and compose poetry there with his guests.
units.literal: From time to time he drank and composed poetry there with guests.

units.zh: 為人有潔癖，盥濯不離手。
units.en: By nature he was fastidiously clean and never stopped washing his hands.
units.literal: By nature he had an obsession with cleanliness and never left off washing his hands.

units.zh: 俗客造廬，比去，必洗滌其處。
units.en: When common visitors came to his lodge, he would wash wherever they had sat as soon as they left.
units.literal: When vulgar guests visited his lodge, as soon as they left he would wash the place where they had been.

units.zh: 求縑素者踵至，瓚亦時應之。
units.en: Those seeking silk scrolls for his paintings came in an endless stream, and Zan would sometimes oblige them.
units.literal: Those seeking silk for painting came one after another, and Zan would sometimes oblige them.

units.zh: 至正初，海內無事，忽散其貲給親故，人咸怪之。
units.en: At the beginning of the Zhizheng era, when the realm was at peace, he suddenly gave away his wealth to relatives and friends, and everyone thought it strange.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Zhizheng era, when the realm was at peace, he suddenly distributed his wealth to relatives and friends, and all thought it strange.

units.zh: 未幾兵興，富家悉被禍，而瓚扁舟箬笠，往來震澤、三泖間，獨不罹患。
units.en: Before long warfare broke out, and wealthy families were ruined one after another. Zan alone, in a small boat and bamboo hat, moved between Lake Zhen and the Three Marshes and suffered no harm.
units.literal: Before long warfare arose; wealthy families all suffered disaster, while Zan in a small boat and bamboo hat traveled between Lake Zhen and the Three Marshes alone untouched by calamity.

units.zh: 張士誠累欲鉤致之，逃漁舟以免。
units.en: Zhang Shicheng repeatedly tried to lure him into service, but he escaped aboard fishing boats to avoid capture.
units.literal: Zhang Shicheng repeatedly wished to lure him in, but he escaped aboard fishing boats to avoid capture.

units.zh: 其弟士信以幣乞畫，瓚又斥去。
units.en: His younger brother Shixin sent gifts begging for a painting, and Zan drove him away once more.
units.literal: His younger brother Shixin sent gifts begging for a painting, and Zan drove him away again.

units.zh: 士信恚，他日從賓客游湖上，聞異香出葭葦間，疑為瓚也，物色漁舟中，果得之。
units.en: Shixin was furious. One day, while touring the lake with his guests, he caught a strange fragrance rising from the reeds, suspected it was Zan, searched the fishing boats, and found him.
units.literal: Shixin was resentful. Another day, while touring the lake with guests, he caught a strange fragrance from among the reeds, suspected it was Zan, searched the fishing boats, and indeed found him.

units.zh: 抶幾斃，終無一言。
units.en: They beat him nearly to death, yet he never uttered a word.
units.literal: He was beaten nearly to death, yet in the end spoke not a word.

units.zh: 及吳平，瓚年老矣，黃冠野服，混跡編氓。
units.en: When Wu was pacified, Zan was already old. In a Daoist cap and rustic dress he mingled among the common people.
units.literal: When Wu was pacified, Zan was already old. In Daoist cap and rustic dress he mingled among the common people.

units.zh: 洪武七年卒，年七十四。
units.en: He died in the seventh year of Hongwu, at the age of seventy-four.
units.literal: He died in the seventh year of Hongwu, aged seventy-four.

units.zh: 徐舫，字方舟，桐廬人。
units.en: Xu Fang, courtesy name Fangzhou, was a native of Tonglu.
units.literal: Xu Fang, styled Fangzhou, was a man of Tonglu.

units.zh: 幼輕俠，好擊劍、走馬、蹴踘。
units.en: In youth he was rakish, fond of swordplay, horse-racing, and cuju.
units.literal: In youth he was rakish, fond of swordplay, horse-racing, and cuju.

units.zh: 既而悔之，習科舉業。
units.en: Later he repented of this and took up examination studies.
units.literal: Later he regretted this and studied for the civil examinations.

units.zh: 已，復棄去，學為歌詩。
units.en: Then he abandoned that as well and turned to writing songs and poetry.
units.literal: Then he abandoned that again and learned to write songs and poetry.

units.zh: 睦故多詩人，唐有方干、徐凝、李頻、施肩吾，宋有高師魯、滕元秀，號睦州詩派，舫悉取步聚之。
units.en: Mu had long produced many poets. In the Tang there were Fang Gan, Xu Ning, Li Pin, and Shi Jianwu; in the Song, Gao Shilu and Teng Yuanxiu—the so-called Muzhou school of poetry—and Fang took them all as models.
units.literal: Mu had long had many poets: in Tang, Fang Gan, Xu Ning, Li Pin, and Shi Jianwu; in Song, Gao Shilu and Teng Yuanxiu—the so-called Muzhou school of poetry—and Fang took them all as models to follow.

units.zh: 既乃游四方，交其名士，詩益工。
units.en: He then traveled widely, befriended celebrated men, and his poetry grew ever more accomplished.
units.literal: Then he traveled the four quarters, befriended famous men, and his poetry grew more accomplished.

units.zh: 行省參政蘇天爵將薦之，舫笑曰：「吾詩人耳，可羈以章紱哉。」
units.en: Su Tianjue, provincial administration commissioner, was about to recommend him. Fang laughed and said: "I am only a poet—how can you bind me with official robes and regalia?"
units.literal: Su Tianjue, provincial administration commissioner, was about to recommend him. Fang laughed and said: "I am but a poet—how can I be bound with official regalia?"

units.zh: 竟避去。
units.en: In the end he slipped away and avoided appointment.
units.literal: In the end he avoided it and left.

units.zh: 築室江皋，日苦吟於雲煙出沒間，翛然若與世隔，因自號滄江散人。
units.en: He built a house on the riverbank and spent his days composing poetry amid drifting mist and cloud, detached as if cut off from the world. He therefore styled himself the Wanderer of the Cang River.
units.literal: He built a house on the riverbank and daily labored at poetry amid clouds appearing and vanishing, detached as if cut off from the world, and so styled himself the Wanderer of the Cang River.

units.zh: 宋濂、劉基、葉琛、章溢之赴召也，舟溯桐江，忽有人黃冠鹿裘立江上，招基而笑，且語侵之。
units.en: When Song Lian, Liu Ji, Ye Chen, and Zhang Yi were traveling to answer the imperial summons, their boat went up the Tong River. Suddenly a man in a yellow cap and deerskin cloak stood on the bank, beckoned to Ji with a laugh, and spoke to him in mocking tones.
units.literal: When Song Lian, Liu Ji, Ye Chen, and Zhang Yi were going to answer the summons, their boat went up the Tong River. Suddenly a man in yellow cap and deerskin cloak stood on the riverbank, beckoned to Ji and laughed, and his words were cutting.

units.zh: 基望見，急延入舟中。
units.en: Ji saw him from afar and hastily invited him aboard.
units.literal: Ji saw him from afar and hastily invited him into the boat.

units.zh: 琛、溢競歡謔，各取冠服服之，欲載上黟川，其人不可乃止。
units.en: Chen and Yi joined in merry banter, each took cap and robe and dressed him in them, and wanted to carry him upriver to Yichuan, but the man refused and they desisted.
units.literal: Chen and Yi vied in merry banter, each took cap and robe and dressed him in them, and wished to carry him up to Yichuan, but the man would not agree and they stopped.

units.zh: 濂初未相識，以問。
units.en: Lian did not know him at first and asked who he was.
units.literal: Lian did not know him at first and asked who he was.

units.zh: 基曰：「此徐方舟也。」
units.en: Ji said: "This is Xu Fangzhou."
units.literal: Ji said: "This is Xu Fangzhou."

units.zh: 濂因起共歡笑，酌酒而別。
units.en: Lian then rose and joined in laughter, poured wine, and they parted.
units.literal: Lian then rose and joined in laughter, poured wine, and they parted.

units.zh: 舫詩有《瑤林》、《滄江》二集。
units.en: Fang's poetry survives in two collections, Yaolin and Cangjiang.
units.literal: Fang's poetry was collected in two works, Yaolin and Cangjiang.

units.zh: 年六十八，丙午春，卒於家。
units.en: He was sixty-eight years old when he died at home in the spring of the bingwu year.
units.literal: Aged sixty-eight, in the spring of the bingwu year, he died at home.

units.zh: 楊恆，字本初，諸暨人。
units.en: Yang Heng, courtesy name Benchu, was a native of Zhuji.
units.literal: Yang Heng, styled Benchu, was a man of Zhuji.

units.zh: 外族方氏建義塾，館四方游學士，恆幼往受諸經，輒領其旨要。
units.en: His mother's clan, the Fang family, built a charity school and housed traveling scholars from every quarter. Heng went there as a boy to study the classics and always grasped their essentials at once.
units.literal: His mother's clan, the Fang, built a charity school and housed traveling scholars from all quarters. Heng went there in youth to study the classics and always grasped their essentials.

units.zh: 文峻潔，有聲郡邑間。
units.en: His writing was austere and refined, and his reputation spread throughout the district.
units.literal: His writing was severe and pure, and he had a reputation throughout the district.

units.zh: 浦江鄭氏延為師，閱十年退居白鹿山，戴棕冠，披羊裘，帶經耕煙雨間，嘯歌自樂，因自號白鹿生。
units.en: The Zheng family of Pujiang invited him to serve as their teacher. After ten years he retired to Bailu Mountain, wore a palm-fiber cap and sheepskin cloak, carried the classics while farming amid mist and rain, and sang for his own delight. He styled himself the Man of White Deer.
units.literal: The Zheng of Pujiang invited him as teacher. After ten years he retired to Bailu Mountain, wore a palm-fiber cap and sheepskin cloak, carried the classics while farming amid mist and rain, sang and rejoiced by himself, and styled himself the Man of White Deer.

units.zh: 太祖既下浙東，命欒鳳知州事。
units.en: After the Taizu had pacified eastern Zhejiang, he appointed Luan Feng to administer the prefecture.
units.literal: After the Taizu had taken eastern Zhejiang, he appointed Luan Feng to administer the prefecture.

units.zh: 鳳請為州學師，恆固讓不起。
units.en: Feng asked him to serve as teacher of the prefectural school, but Heng firmly declined and would not accept.
units.literal: Feng asked him to be teacher of the prefectural school, but Heng firmly declined and would not rise to serve.

units.zh: 鳳乃命州中子弟即家問道。
units.en: Feng then ordered the young men of the prefecture to come to Heng's home to study the Way.
units.literal: Feng then ordered the young men of the prefecture to seek the Way at his home.

units.zh: 政有缺失，輒貽書咨訪。
units.en: Whenever governance fell short, Feng would send letters seeking his counsel.
units.literal: When governance had shortcomings, he would send letters to consult him.

units.zh: 後唐鐸知紹興，欲辟起之，復固辭。
units.en: Later, when Tang Duo governed Shaoxing, he wished to summon Heng to office, but Heng again firmly declined.
units.literal: Later Tang Duo governed Shaoxing and wished to summon him to office, but he again firmly declined.

units.zh: 宋濂之為學士也，擬薦為國子師，聞不受州郡辟命，乃已。
units.en: When Song Lian became a Hanlin academician, he planned to recommend Heng as teacher of the National University, but hearing that he would accept no appointment from prefecture or district, he let the matter drop.
units.literal: When Song Lian became a Hanlin academician, he planned to recommend Heng as teacher of the National University, but hearing that he would not accept summons from prefectures and districts, he dropped the matter.

units.zh: 恆性醇篤，與人語，出肺肝相示。
units.en: Heng was by nature sincere and earnest; in conversation he laid bare his heart without reserve.
units.literal: Heng's nature was sincere and earnest; in speaking with others he laid bare heart and liver.

units.zh: 事稍乖名義，輒峻言指斥。
units.en: Whenever a matter fell even slightly short of right principle, he would rebuke it in stern words.
units.literal: When matters slightly violated right principle, he would sternly rebuke them in speech.

units.zh: 家無儋石，而臨財甚介，鄉人奉為楷法焉。
units.en: His household held scarcely a bushel of grain, yet he was scrupulous in the face of wealth, and the villagers took him as their standard of conduct.
units.literal: His household had not a dan of grain, yet facing wealth he was very scrupulous; the villagers took him as their model.

units.zh: 時有陳洄者，義烏人。
units.en: At the time there was also Chen Hui, a native of Yiwu.
units.literal: At the time there was Chen Hui, a man of Yiwu.

units.zh: 幼治經，長通百家言。
units.en: In youth he studied the classics; as an adult he mastered the teachings of the hundred schools.
units.literal: In youth he studied the classics; grown, he mastered the teachings of the hundred schools.

units.zh: 初欲以功名顯，既而隱居，戴青霞冠，披白鹿裘，不復與塵事接。
units.en: At first he wished to win fame through official achievement; later he withdrew from the world, wore the azure-cloud cap and white-deer cloak, and would have no more dealings with worldly affairs.
units.literal: At first he wished to distinguish himself through fame and merit; later he went into seclusion, wore the azure-cloud cap and white-deer cloak, and no longer had dealings with worldly affairs.

units.zh: 所居近大溪，多修竹，自號竹溪逸民。
units.en: His dwelling lay beside a great stream surrounded by tall bamboo, and he styled himself the Recluse of Bamboo Stream.
units.literal: His dwelling was near a great stream with many tall bamboo, and he styled himself the Recluse of Bamboo Stream.

units.zh: 常乘小艇，吹短簫，吹已，叩舷而歌，悠然自適。
units.en: He often took a small boat, played a short flute, and when he finished would strike the gunwale and sing, utterly content in his own world.
units.literal: He often rode a small boat, played a short flute, and when finished struck the gunwale and sang, content and at ease.

units.zh: 宋濂俱為之傳。
units.en: Song Lian wrote biographies for both Yang Heng and Chen Hui.
units.literal: Song Lian wrote biographies for both of them.

units.zh: 楊引，吉水人。
units.en: Yang Yin was a native of Jishui.
units.literal: Yang Yin, a man of Jishui.

units.zh: 好學能詩文，為宋濂、陶安所稱。
units.en: He loved learning and was accomplished in poetry and prose, and was praised by Song Lian and Tao An.
units.literal: Fond of learning and skilled in poetry and prose, he was praised by Song Lian and Tao An.

units.zh: 駙馬都尉陸賢從受學，入朝，舉止端雅。
units.en: The imperial son-in-law Lu Xian studied under him, and when Xian entered court his bearing was dignified and refined.
units.literal: The imperial son-in-law Lu Xian studied under him; when he entered court his bearing was dignified and refined.

units.zh: 太祖喜，問誰教者，賢以引對，立召見，賜食。
units.en: The Taizu was pleased and asked who had taught him. Xian named Yin, and Yin was immediately summoned to audience and given a meal.
units.literal: The Taizu was pleased and asked who had taught him. Xian named Yin in reply, and Yin was immediately summoned and given food.

units.zh: 他日，賢以褻服見，引太息曰：「是其心易我，不可久居此矣。」
units.en: Another day Xian came to see him in informal dress. Yin sighed deeply and said: "His heart has turned away from me—I cannot remain here much longer."
units.literal: Another day Xian came to see him in informal dress. Yin sighed deeply and said: "His heart has changed toward me—I cannot remain here long."

units.zh: 復以纂修征，亦不就。
units.en: When he was summoned again to join the compilation project, he again refused.
units.literal: He was again summoned for compilation work, but again would not go.

units.zh: 其教學者，先操履而後文藝。
units.en: In teaching his students, he put conduct before literary accomplishment.
units.literal: In teaching his students, he put conduct first and literary accomplishment after.

units.zh: 嘗揭《論語鄉黨》篇示人曰：「吾教自有養生術，安事偃仰吐納為。」
units.en: He once displayed the Xiangdang chapter of the Analects to others and said: "My teaching has its own way of nurturing life—why bother with breathing exercises and postures?"
units.literal: He once displayed the Xiangdang chapter of the Analects to others and said: "My teaching has its own method of nurturing life—why bother with lying down and breathing exercises?"

units.zh: 乃節飲食，時動息，迄老視聽不衰。
units.en: He regulated his food and drink and kept regular movement and rest, and to the end of his life his sight and hearing never failed.
units.literal: He then regulated food and drink and kept regular movement and rest; to old age his sight and hearing did not decline.

units.zh: 既歿，安福劉球稱其學探道原，文范後世，去就出處，卓然有陶潛、徐穉之風。
units.en: After his death, Liu Qiu of Anfu praised his learning for probing the origin of the Way, his writing as a model for later ages, and his conduct in withdrawal and emergence as bearing the unmistakable spirit of Tao Qian and Xu Zhi.
units.literal: After his death Liu Qiu of Anfu praised his learning as probing the origin of the Way, his writing as a model for later ages, and his withdrawal and emergence as markedly bearing the spirit of Tao Qian and Xu Zhi.

units.zh: 吳海，字朝宗，閩縣人。
units.en: Wu Hai, courtesy name Chaozong, was a native of Min County.
units.literal: Wu Hai, styled Chaozong, was a man of Min County.

units.zh: 元季以學行稱。
units.en: In the late Yuan he was famed for learning and conduct.
units.literal: In the late Yuan he was famed for learning and conduct.

units.zh: 值四方盜起，絕意仕進。
units.en: When bandits rose throughout the realm, he abandoned all thought of an official career.
units.literal: When bandits rose in all quarters, he utterly abandoned any wish to advance in office.

units.zh: 洪武初，守臣欲薦諸朝，力辭免。
units.en: In the early Hongwu period the local officials wished to recommend him to court, but he firmly declined.
units.literal: In the early Hongwu period the local officials wished to recommend him to court, but he firmly declined and was excused.

units.zh: 既而徵詣史局，復力辭。
units.en: Later he was summoned to the historiography bureau and again firmly declined.
units.literal: Later he was summoned to the historiography bureau and again firmly declined.

units.zh: 嘗言：「楊、墨、釋、老，聖道之賊，管、商、申、韓，治道之賊，稗官野乘，正史之賊，支詞艷說，文章之賊。
units.en: He once said: "Yang Zhu, Mozi, Buddhism, and Daoism are enemies of the sage's Way; Guan Zhong, Shang Yang, Shen Buhai, and Han Fei are enemies of good governance; unofficial histories and wild records are enemies of orthodox history; florid and seductive writings are enemies of true literature.
units.literal: He once said: "Yang Zhu, Mozi, Buddhism, and Daoism are thieves of the sage's Way; Guan Zhong, Shang Yang, Shen Buhai, and Han Fei are thieves of the way of governance; unofficial histories and wild records are thieves of the orthodox histories; florid words and seductive writings are thieves of literature.

units.zh: 上之人，宜敕通經大臣，會諸儒定其品目，頒之天下，民間非此不得輒藏，坊市不得輒粥。
units.en: Those in authority should order great ministers versed in the classics to assemble the Confucian scholars, fix the approved categories of books, and promulgate them throughout the realm, so that the people may not keep what is not on the list and markets may not sell what is forbidden.
units.literal: Those above should order great ministers versed in the classics to assemble the Confucians, fix categories of books, promulgate them throughout the realm, forbid the people to keep what is not on the list, and forbid markets to sell them.

units.zh: 如是數年，學者生長不涉異聞，其於養德育才，豈曰小補。」
units.en: If this were done for several years, scholars would grow up untouched by heterodox learning. In nurturing virtue and forming talent, would this not be a great benefit?"
units.literal: If this were done for several years, scholars would grow up untouched by heterodox learning—in nurturing virtue and forming talent, would this not be a great benefit?"

units.zh: 因著書一編曰《書禍》，以發明之。
units.en: He therefore wrote a book in one fascicle called Writings as Calamity to expound this view.
units.literal: He therefore wrote a book in one fascicle called Writings as Calamity to expound this.

units.zh: 與永福王翰善。
units.en: He was on good terms with Wang Han of Yongfu.
units.literal: He was on good terms with Wang Han of Yongfu.

units.zh: 翰嘗仕元，海數勸之死，翰果自裁。
units.en: Han had once served the Yuan. Hai repeatedly urged him to take his own life, and Han did so.
units.literal: Han had once served the Yuan; Hai repeatedly urged him to die, and Han indeed took his own life.

units.zh: 海教養其子偁，卒底成立。
units.en: Hai raised and educated Han's son Cheng, who in the end grew into a fully accomplished man.
units.literal: Hai taught and raised his son Cheng, who in the end was fully established.

units.zh: 平居虛懷樂善，有規過者，欣然立改，因顏其齋曰聞過。
units.en: In daily life he was open-minded and delighted in doing good. When someone pointed out a fault, he gladly corrected it at once, and named his study Hearing Fault.
units.literal: In ordinary life he was open-minded and delighted in goodness; when someone corrected his faults he gladly changed at once, and so he named his studio Hearing Fault.

units.zh: 為文嚴整典雅，一歸諸理，後學咸宗仰之。
units.en: His writing was austere, orderly, and elegant, always grounded in principle, and later students all looked up to him as a model.
units.literal: His writing was severe, orderly, and elegant, all returning to principle; later students all looked up to him as a model.

units.zh: 有《聞過齋集》行世。
units.en: His collected works, the Hearing Fault Studio Collection, circulated in his day.
units.literal: His collected works from the Hearing Fault Studio circulated in the world.

units.zh: 劉閔，字子賢，莆田人。
units.en: Liu Min, courtesy name Zixian, was a native of Putian.
units.literal: Liu Min, styled Zixian, was a man of Putian.

units.zh: 生而純愨。
units.en: From birth he was pure and sincere.
units.literal: From birth he was pure and sincere.

units.zh: 早孤，絕意科舉，求古聖賢禔躬訓家之法，率而行之。
units.en: Orphaned early, he abandoned the civil examinations, sought out the ways in which ancient sages cultivated themselves and instructed their households, and followed them in all things.
units.literal: Orphaned early, he abandoned the civil examinations, sought the methods by which ancient sages cultivated the person and instructed the family, and followed them in all things.

units.zh: 祖母及父喪未舉，斷酒肉，遠室家。
units.en: His grandmother and father had died but their funerals had not yet been performed. He abstained from wine and meat and kept away from wife and home.
units.literal: His grandmother and father had died but funerals had not yet been held; he abstained from wine and meat and kept far from wife and home.

units.zh: 訓鄰邑，朔望歸，則號哭殯所，如是三年。
units.en: He taught in a neighboring district, but on the first and fifteenth of each month he returned home and wailed at the place where the coffins lay. He did this for three years.
units.literal: He taught in a neighboring district; on the first and fifteenth of each month he returned and wailed at the place of the coffin, doing so for three years.

units.zh: 婦失愛於母，出之，獨居奉養，疾不解衣。
units.en: When his wife fell out of his mother's favor, he sent her away and lived alone to care for his mother. When his mother was ill, he never removed his clothes.
units.literal: His wife lost his mother's favor and he sent her away; he lived alone in serving his mother, and when she was ill he did not remove his clothes.

units.zh: 母或恚怒，則整衣竟夕跪榻前。
units.en: When his mother grew angry, he would straighten his clothes and kneel all night before her couch.
units.literal: When his mother was angry, he would straighten his clothes and kneel all night before her couch.

units.zh: 祭享奠獻，一循古禮，鄉人莫不欽重。
units.en: In sacrifices and offerings he followed the ancient rites in every detail, and the villagers all held him in reverence.
units.literal: In sacrifices, offerings, and presentations he followed the ancient rites in all things; the villagers all held him in reverence.

units.zh: 副使羅璟立社學，構養親堂，延閔為師。
units.en: Vice Commissioner Luo Jing established a community school, built a Hall for Nurturing Parents, and invited Min to serve as teacher.
units.literal: Vice Commissioner Luo Jing established a community school, built a Hall for Nurturing Parents, and invited Min as teacher.

units.zh: 提學僉事周孟中捐俸助養。
units.en: Education Intendant Zhou Mengzhong donated his salary to help support Min's mother.
units.literal: Education Intendant Zhou Mengzhong donated his salary to help support him.

units.zh: 知府王弼每祭廟社，必延致齋居，曰：「此人在座，私意自消。」
units.en: Whenever Prefect Wang Bi performed sacrifices at the temple and altar of soil and grain, he would invite Min to join him in ritual fasting, saying: "With this man present, private motives naturally vanish."
units.literal: Prefect Wang Bi, whenever he sacrificed at the temple and altar of soil and grain, would invite Min to dwell in fasting purity, saying: "With this man present, private motives naturally vanish."

units.zh: 置田二十余畝贍之，並受不辭。
units.en: Wang set aside more than twenty mu of fields to support him, and Min accepted the gift without declining.
units.literal: He set aside more than twenty mu of fields to support him, and Min accepted both without declining.

units.zh: 及母歿，即送田還官，廬墓三年。
units.en: When his mother died, he immediately returned the fields to the government and lived in a mourning hut beside her tomb for three years.
units.literal: When his mother died, he immediately returned the fields to the government and lived in a hut by her tomb for three years.

units.zh: 弟婦求分產，閔闔戶自撾，婦感悟乃已。
units.en: His younger brother's wife sought to divide the family property. Min shut the door and beat himself in remonstrance, and the woman, moved to repentance, desisted.
units.literal: His younger brother's wife sought to divide the property; Min shut the door and beat himself, and the wife, moved to understanding, stopped.

units.zh: 弘治中，僉都御史林俊上言：「伏見皇太子年逾幼學，習處宮中，罕接外傅，豫教之道似為未備。
units.en: During the Hongzhi reign, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Lin Jun memorialized: "I observe that the Crown Prince has passed the age for early learning. Accustomed to life in the palace, he rarely receives tutelage from outside masters, and the way of advance instruction seems not yet complete.
units.literal: During the Hongzhi reign, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Lin Jun memorialized: "I observe that the Crown Prince has passed the age for early learning. Accustomed to life in the palace, he rarely receives tutelage from outside masters, and the way of advance instruction appears not yet complete.

units.zh: 今講讀侍從諸臣固已簡用，然百司眾職，山林隱逸，不謂無人。
units.en: Though the lecturing, reading, and attendant ministers have already been selected, among the myriad offices and posts, and among the recluses of mountain and forest, it cannot be said that there are no capable men.
units.literal: Though the lecturing, reading, and attendant ministers have now been selected, among the myriad offices and posts, and among the recluses of mountain and forest, it cannot be said that there are no capable men.

units.zh: 以臣所知，則禮部侍郎謝鐸、太僕少卿儲巏、光祿少卿楊廉，可備講員。
units.en: To my knowledge, Vice Minister of Rites Xie Duo, Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud Chu Guan, and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Yang Lian are fit to serve as lecturers.
units.literal: To my knowledge, Vice Minister of Rites Xie Duo, Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud Chu Guan, and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Yang Lian may serve as lecturers.

units.zh: 其資序未合，德行可取者二人，則致仕副使曹時中、布衣劉閔是也。
units.en: Of those whose rank and seniority do not yet qualify but whose conduct is worthy, there are two men: retired Vice Commissioner Cao Shizhong and the commoner Liu Min.
units.literal: Of those whose rank and seniority do not yet qualify but whose conduct is worthy, there are two: retired Vice Commissioner Cao Shizhong and the commoner Liu Min.

units.zh: 閔，臣縣人，恭慎醇粹，孝行高古。
units.en: Min is a man of my native district—respectful, cautious, pure, and sincere, with filial conduct of the highest antiquity.
units.literal: Min is a man of my native district—respectful, cautious, pure, and sincere, with filial conduct of the highest antiquity.

units.zh: 日無二粥，身無完衣，處之晏如。
units.en: He takes but one meal a day and wears no whole garment, yet bears it with perfect composure.
units.literal: He takes but one meal a day and wears no whole garment, yet bears it with perfect ease.

units.zh: 監司劉大夏、徐貫等恆敬禮之。
units.en: The surveillance commissioners Liu Daxia, Xu Guan, and others constantly treat him with ritual respect.
units.literal: The surveillance commissioners Liu Daxia, Xu Guan, and others constantly treat him with ritual respect.

units.zh: 臣謂可禮致時中為宮僚，閔以布衣入侍，必能涵育薰陶，裨益睿質。」
units.en: I submit that Cao Shizhong may be invited by ritual to serve as a palace aide, and that Min may enter attendance as a commoner—they will surely nurture and refine the heir, benefiting his sagely character."
units.literal: I submit that Cao Shizhong may be invited by ritual to serve as a palace aide, and Min may enter attendance as a commoner—they will surely nurture and refine the heir, benefiting his sagely character."

units.zh: 時不能用。
units.en: At the time the court did not adopt his proposal.
units.literal: At the time the court did not adopt his proposal.

units.zh: 其後，巡按御史宗彝、饒瑭欲援詔例舉閔經明行修，閔力辭。
units.en: Later, touring censors Zong Yi and Rao Tang wished to invoke the edict precedent to recommend Min for classic learning and upright conduct, but Min firmly declined.
units.literal: Later, touring censors Zong Yi and Rao Tang wished to invoke the edict precedent to recommend Min for classic learning and upright conduct, but Min firmly declined.

units.zh: 知府陳效請遂其志，榮以學職。
units.en: Prefect Chen Xiao asked that his wish be granted and honored him with a school appointment.
units.literal: Prefect Chen Xiao asked that his wish be granted and honored him with a school post.

units.zh: 正德元年，遙授儒學訓導。
units.en: In the first year of the Zhengde reign, he received a remote appointment as instructor in the Confucian school.
units.literal: In the first year of the Zhengde reign, he was appointed from afar as instructor in the Confucian school.

units.zh: 楊黼，雲南太和人也。
units.en: Yang Fu was a native of Taihe in Yunnan.
units.literal: Yang Fu, a man of Taihe in Yunnan.

units.zh: 好學，讀《五經》皆百遍。
units.en: He loved learning and read each of the Five Classics a hundred times.
units.literal: Fond of learning, he read each of the Five Classics a hundred times.

units.zh: 工篆籀，好釋典。
units.en: He was skilled in seal and ancient script and fond of Buddhist scriptures.
units.literal: He was skilled in seal and ancient script and fond of Buddhist scriptures.

units.zh: 或勸其應舉，笑曰：「不理性命，理外物耶？」
units.en: When someone urged him to take the civil examinations, he laughed and said: "If one does not put one's nature and fate in order, is one putting external things in order?"
units.literal: When someone urged him to take the examinations, he laughed and said: "If one does not order one's nature and fate, is one ordering external things?"

units.zh: 庭前有大桂樹，縛板樹上，題曰桂樓。
units.en: Before his courtyard stood a great cassia tree. He bound boards in its branches and inscribed it Cassia Tower.
units.literal: Before the courtyard stood a great cassia tree; he bound boards in the tree and inscribed it Cassia Tower.

units.zh: 偃仰其中，歌詩自得。
units.en: He lay back within it, singing poetry in perfect contentment.
units.literal: He lay back within it, singing poetry in contentment.

units.zh: 躬耕數畝供甘膬，但求親悅，不顧余也。
units.en: He personally farmed several mu to provide savory food for his parents, seeking only their delight and caring for nothing else.
units.literal: He personally farmed several mu to supply savory delicacies, seeking only his parents' delight and caring for nothing else.

units.zh: 注《孝經》數萬言，證群書，根性命，字皆小篆。
units.en: He annotated the Classic of Filial Piety in tens of thousands of words, citing books from every tradition and grounding it in nature and fate. Every character was written in small seal script.
units.literal: He annotated the Classic of Filial Piety in tens of thousands of words, citing all books and rooting it in nature and fate; every character was in small seal script.

units.zh: 所用硯乾，將下樓取水，硯池忽滿，自是為常，時人咸異之。
units.en: Once, when his inkstone had dried and he was about to go downstairs for water, the ink pool suddenly filled. After that it happened constantly, and people of the time all marveled at it.
units.literal: The inkstone he used had dried; as he was about to go downstairs for water, the ink pool suddenly filled. From then on this was constant, and people of the time all thought it strange.

units.zh: 父母歿，為傭營葬畢，入雞足，棲羅漢壁石窟山十餘年，壽至八十。
units.en: When his parents died he worked as a hired laborer until their burial was complete, then entered Chicken Foot Mountain and lived in the stone grottoes of Luohan Cliff for more than ten years. He lived to the age of eighty.
units.literal: When his parents died he worked as a hired laborer until their burial was complete, then entered Chicken Foot Mountain and dwelt at the stone grottoes of Luohan Cliff for more than ten years, living to eighty.

units.zh: 子遜迎歸，一日沐浴，令子孫拜，曰：「明日吾行矣。」
units.en: His son Xun welcomed him home. One day he bathed, had his descendants bow before him, and said: "Tomorrow I depart."
units.literal: His son Xun welcomed him home. One day he bathed, had his descendants bow, and said: "Tomorrow I depart."

units.zh: 果卒。
units.en: And so he died.
units.literal: He indeed died.

units.zh: 孫一元
units.en: Sun Yiyuan
units.literal: Sun Yiyuan

units.zh: 孫一元，字太初，不知何許人，問其邑里，曰：「我秦人也。」
units.en: Sun Yiyuan, courtesy name Taichu, was of unknown origin. When asked where he came from, he said: "I am a man of Qin."
units.literal: Sun Yiyuan, styled Taichu, was of unknown origin; asked about his native place, he said: "I am a man of Qin."

units.zh: 嘗棲太白之巔，故號太白山人。
units.en: He once lived on the summit of Mount Taibai and therefore styled himself the Man of Taibai Mountain.
units.literal: He once dwelt on the summit of Taibai and therefore styled himself the Man of Taibai Mountain.

units.zh: 或曰安化王宗人，王坐不軌誅，故變姓名避難也。
units.en: Some say he was a clansman of the Prince of Anhua. When the prince was executed for sedition, he changed his name to escape persecution.
units.literal: Some say he was a clansman of the Prince of Anhua; the prince was executed for sedition, and so he changed his name to avoid disaster.

units.zh: 一元姿性絕人，善為詩，風儀秀朗，蹤跡奇譎，烏巾白帢，攜鐵笛鶴瓢，遍游中原，東逾齊、魯，南涉江、淮，歷荊抵吳越，所至賦詩，談神仙，論當世事，往往傾其座人。
units.en: Yiyuan's gifts were extraordinary. He was skilled in poetry, his bearing elegant and bright, his tracks strange and uncanny. In a black cap and white headcloth, carrying an iron flute and a wine gourd, he traveled throughout the central plains, east beyond Qi and Lu, south across the Yangtze and Huai, through Jing to Wu and Yue. Wherever he went he composed poetry, spoke of immortals, and discussed affairs of the age, often overwhelming everyone seated with him.
units.literal: Yiyuan's natural gifts were extraordinary; he was skilled in poetry, his bearing elegant and bright, his tracks strange and uncanny. In black cap and white headcloth, carrying an iron flute and a gourd, he traveled throughout the central plains, east beyond Qi and Lu, south across the Yangtze and Huai, through Jing to Wu and Yue. Wherever he went he composed poetry, spoke of immortals, and discussed affairs of the age, often overwhelming those seated with him.

units.zh: 鉛山費宏罷相，訪之杭州南屏山，值其晝寢，就臥內與語。
units.en: Fei Hong of Qianshan, having left the chancellorship, visited him at Nanping Mountain in Hangzhou. Finding him asleep in broad daylight, Hong spoke with him there in his bed.
units.literal: Fei Hong of Qianshan, having left the chancellorship, visited him at Nanping Mountain in Hangzhou, found him asleep by day, and spoke with him inside his bed.

units.zh: 送之及門，了不酬答。
units.en: When Yiyuan escorted him to the door, he made no reply at all.
units.literal: When Hong saw him to the door, he made no reply at all.

units.zh: 宏出語人曰：「吾一生未嘗見此人。」
units.en: Hong went out and told others: "In all my life I have never met a man like this."
units.literal: Hong went out and told others: "In all my life I have never met a man like this."

units.zh: 時劉麟以知府罷歸，龍霓以僉事謝政，並客湖州，與郡人故御史陵昆善，而長興吳珫隱居好客，三人者並主於其家。
units.en: At the time Liu Lin had returned home after leaving office as prefect, and Long Ni had retired from his post as commissioner. Both were staying in Huzhou and were friendly with the former censor Ling Kun of the prefecture, while Wu Qiong of Changxing lived in seclusion and loved to entertain guests. The three all lodged as guests in Qiong's home.
units.literal: At the time Liu Lin had returned home after leaving office as prefect, and Long Ni had retired from his post as commissioner; both were guests in Huzhou. They were friendly with the former censor Ling Kun of the prefecture, while Wu Qiong of Changxing lived in seclusion and loved guests. The three all presided as hosts in his home.

units.zh: 珫因招一元入社，稱「苕溪五隱」。
units.en: Qiong therefore invited Yiyuan into their circle and called them the "Five Recluses of Tiaoxi."
units.literal: Qiong therefore invited Yiyuan into their society and called them the "Five Recluses of Tiaoxi."

units.zh: 一元買田溪上，將老焉。
units.en: Yiyuan bought fields beside the stream and planned to grow old there.
units.literal: Yiyuan bought fields by the stream and planned to grow old there.

units.zh: 舉人施侃雅善一元，妻以妻妹張氏，生一女而卒，年止三十七。
units.en: The juren Shi Kan was on excellent terms with Yiyuan and gave him his wife's younger sister, née Zhang, in marriage. She bore a daughter and then died. Yiyuan was only thirty-seven.
units.literal: The juren Shi Kan was on excellent terms with Yiyuan and gave him his wife's younger sister, née Zhang, in marriage. She bore a daughter and then died; Yiyuan was only thirty-seven.

units.zh: 珫等葬之道場山。
units.en: Qiong and the others buried him on Mount Daochang.
units.literal: Qiong and the others buried him on Mount Daochang.

units.zh: 沈周，字啟南，長洲人。
units.en: Shen Zhou, courtesy name Qinan, was a native of Changzhou.
units.literal: Shen Zhou, styled Qinan, was a man of Changzhou.

units.zh: 祖澄，永樂間舉人材，不就。
units.en: His grandfather Cheng was recommended as a man of talent in the Yongle era but refused to accept office.
units.literal: His grandfather Cheng was recommended as a man of talent in the Yongle era but would not accept office.

units.zh: 所居曰西庄，日置酒款賓，人擬之顧仲瑛。
units.en: His dwelling was called West Manor. Each day he set out wine to entertain guests, and people compared him to Gu Zhongying.
units.literal: His dwelling was called West Manor; daily he set out wine to entertain guests, and people compared him to Gu Zhongying.

units.zh: 伯父貞吉，父恆吉，並抗隱。
units.en: His father's elder brother Zhenji and his father Hengji both refused office and lived in seclusion.
units.literal: His father's elder brother Zhenji and his father Hengji both resisted office and lived in seclusion.

units.zh: 構有竹居，兄弟讀書其中。
units.en: They built the Bamboo Dwelling, where the brothers studied together.
units.literal: They built the Bamboo Dwelling, and the brothers studied there.

units.zh: 工詩善畫，臧獲亦解文墨。
units.en: They were skilled in poetry and painting, and even the household servants understood letters and brushwork.
units.literal: Skilled in poetry and good at painting, even the servants understood letters and brushwork.

units.zh: 邑人陳孟賢者，陳五經繼之子也。
units.en: A townsman named Chen Mengxian was the son of Chen Ji, master of the Five Classics.
units.literal: A townsman named Chen Mengxian was the son of Chen Jizhi, the Five Classics master.

units.zh: 周少從之游，得其指授。
units.en: Zhou studied under him in youth and received his instruction.
units.literal: Zhou in youth studied under him and received his instruction.

units.zh: 年十一，游南都，作百韻詩，上巡撫侍郎崔恭。
units.en: At the age of eleven he traveled to the southern capital, composed a poem in a hundred rhymes, and presented it to Surveillance Commissioner Cui Gong.
units.literal: At eleven he traveled to the southern capital, composed a poem in a hundred rhymes, and presented it to the surveillance commissioner Cui Gong.

units.zh: 面試《鳳凰台賦》，援筆立就，恭大嗟異。
units.en: Gong tested him in person on the Rhapsody of Phoenix Terrace. Zhou took up the brush and finished at once, and Gong marveled greatly.
units.literal: Gong tested him face to face on the Rhapsody of Phoenix Terrace; he took up the brush and finished at once, and Gong greatly marveled.

units.zh: 及長，書無所不覽。
units.en: When he grew up, there was no book he did not read.
units.literal: When grown, there was no book he did not read.

units.zh: 文摹左氏，詩擬白居易、蘇軾、陸游，字仿黃庭堅，併為世所愛重。
units.en: His prose modeled Zuo Qiuming, his poetry Bai Juyi, Su Shi, and Lu You, and his calligraphy Huang Tingjian. All were loved and esteemed in his day.
units.literal: His prose modeled Zuo Qiuming, his poetry Bai Juyi, Su Shi, and Lu You, his calligraphy Huang Tingjian—all were loved and esteemed by the age.

units.zh: 尤工於畫，評者謂為明世第一。
units.en: He was especially skilled in painting, and critics called him the finest painter of the Ming age.
units.literal: He was especially skilled in painting; critics called him the first of the Ming age.

units.zh: 郡守欲薦周賢良，周筮《易》，得《遁》之九五，遂決意隱遁。
units.en: The prefect wished to recommend Zhou as a worthy and able man. Zhou divined with the Book of Changes and obtained the fifth line of Dun, and so resolved to withdraw from the world.
units.literal: The prefect wished to recommend Zhou as a worthy and able man. Zhou divined with the Changes and obtained the fifth line of Dun, and so resolved to withdraw into seclusion.

units.zh: 所居有水竹亭館之勝，圖書鼎彝充牣錯列，四方名士過從無虛日，風流文彩，照映一時。
units.en: His dwelling had the beauty of water, bamboo, pavilions, and halls. Books, bronzes, and ritual vessels filled it in profusion. Famous men from every quarter visited without a vacant day, and his elegant literary brilliance illuminated the age.
units.literal: His dwelling had the beauty of water, bamboo, pavilions, and halls; books, tripods, and ritual vessels filled it in profusion. Famous men from all quarters visited without a vacant day; his elegant literary brilliance illuminated the age.

units.zh: 奉親至孝。
units.en: In serving his parents he was supremely filial.
units.literal: In serving his parents he was supremely filial.

units.zh: 父歿，或勸之仕，對曰：「若不知母氏以我為命耶？
units.en: When his father died, some urged him to take office. He replied: "Do you not know that my mother lives for me alone?
units.literal: When his father died, some urged him to take office. He replied: "Do you not know that my mother takes me as her very life?

units.zh: 奈何離膝下。」
units.en: How could I leave her side?"
units.literal: How could I leave her side?"

units.zh: 居恆厭入城市，於郭外置行窩，有事一造之。
units.en: He always disliked entering the city and set up a traveling hut outside the wall. When he had business in town, he would go there only once.
units.literal: He always disliked entering the city and set up a traveling hut outside the wall; when he had business he would go there once.

units.zh: 晚年，匿跡惟恐不深，先後巡撫王恕、彭禮咸禮敬之，欲留幕下，並以母老辭。
units.en: In his later years he hid his tracks, fearing they were not deep enough. The surveillance commissioners Wang Shu and Peng Li in succession treated him with ritual respect and wished to keep him on their staffs, but he declined both on the grounds that his mother was old.
units.literal: In his later years he hid his tracks, fearing they were not deep enough. The surveillance commissioners Wang Shu and Peng Li in succession treated him with ritual respect and wished to keep him in their staffs, but he declined both on the grounds that his mother was old.

units.zh: 有郡守征畫工繪屋壁。
units.en: A prefect summoned painters to decorate the walls of a building.
units.literal: A prefect summoned painters to decorate the walls of a building.

units.zh: 裡人疾周者，入其姓名，遂被攝。
units.en: A villager who bore ill will toward Zhou entered his name on the roster, and Zhou was seized for corvée labor.
units.literal: A villager who bore ill will toward Zhou entered his name, and Zhou was seized for labor service.

units.zh: 或勸周謁貴游以免，周曰：「往役，義也，謁貴游，不更辱乎！」
units.en: Some urged Zhou to visit powerful patrons to escape service. Zhou said: "Going to perform labor is one's duty. Visiting powerful patrons—would that not be a greater shame?"
units.literal: Some urged Zhou to visit powerful patrons to escape service. Zhou said: "Going to labor is duty; visiting powerful patrons—would that not be greater shame?"

units.zh: 卒供役而還。
units.en: In the end he completed the labor service and returned home.
units.literal: In the end he completed the service and returned.

units.zh: 已而守入覲，銓曹問曰：「沈先生無恙乎？」
units.en: Later the prefect went to audience in the capital, and the Board of Personnel asked: "Is Master Shen well?"
units.literal: Later the prefect went to audience in the capital, and the Board of Personnel asked: "Is Master Shen well?"

units.zh: 守不知所對，漫應曰：「無恙。」
units.en: The prefect did not know how to answer and casually replied: "He is well."
units.literal: The prefect did not know how to answer and casually replied: "He is well."

units.zh: 見內閣，李東陽曰：「沈先生有牘乎？」
units.en: When he met the Grand Secretariat, Li Dongyang said: "Has Master Shen sent a memorial?"
units.literal: Meeting the Grand Secretariat, Li Dongyang said: "Has Master Shen sent a memorial?"

units.zh: 守益愕，復漫應曰：「有而未至。」
units.en: The prefect was still more astonished and again answered casually: "There is one, but it has not yet arrived."
units.literal: The prefect was still more astonished and again answered casually: "There is one, but it has not yet arrived."

units.zh: 守出，倉皇謁侍郎吳寬，問「沈先生何人？」
units.en: After leaving the audience, the prefect hurried to visit Vice Minister Wu Kuan and asked: "Who is Master Shen?"
units.literal: Leaving the audience, the prefect hurried to visit Vice Minister Wu Kuan and asked: "Who is Master Shen?"

units.zh: 寬備言其狀。
units.en: Kuan described him in full detail.
units.literal: Kuan fully described his condition.

units.zh: 詢左右，乃畫壁生也。
units.en: Inquiring of those beside him, the prefect learned that he was the wall-painting laborer.
units.literal: Inquiring of those beside him, he learned that he was the wall-painting laborer.

units.zh: 比還，謁周舍，再拜引咎，索飯，飯之而去。
units.en: When he returned home, he visited Zhou's house, bowed twice and acknowledged his fault, asked for a meal, was fed, and left.
units.literal: When he returned, he visited Zhou's house, bowed twice and acknowledged his fault, asked for a meal, was fed, and left.

units.zh: 周以母故，終身不遠游。
units.en: Because of his mother, Zhou never traveled far in all his life.
units.literal: Because of his mother, Zhou never traveled far in all his life.

units.zh: 母年九十九而終，周亦八十矣。
units.en: His mother died at the age of ninety-nine, and Zhou was also eighty.
units.literal: His mother died at ninety-nine, and Zhou was also eighty.

units.zh: 又三年，以正德四年卒。
units.en: Three years later, in the fourth year of Zhengde, he died.
units.literal: Three years later, in the fourth year of Zhengde, he died.

units.zh: 陳繼儒
units.en: Chen Jiru
units.literal: Chen Jiru

units.zh: 陳繼儒，字仲醇，松江華亭人。
units.en: Chen Jiru, courtesy name Zhongchun, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.
units.literal: Chen Jiru, styled Zhongchun, was a man of Huating in Songjiang.

units.zh: 幼穎異，能文章，同郡徐階特器重之。
units.en: In youth he was exceptionally bright and able to write essays. Xu Jie of the same prefecture especially valued him.
units.literal: In youth he was exceptionally bright and able to write essays; Xu Jie of the same prefecture especially valued him.

units.zh: 長為諸生，與董其昌齊名。
units.en: As an adult he became a student and was equally famed with Dong Qichang.
units.literal: Grown, he became a student and was equally famed with Dong Qichang.

units.zh: 太倉王錫爵招與子衡讀書支硎山。
units.en: Wang Xijue of Taicang invited him to study on Mount Zhijin with his son Heng.
units.literal: Wang Xijue of Taicang invited him to study on Mount Zhijin with his son Heng.

units.zh: 王世貞亦雅重繼儒，三吳名下士爭欲得為師友。
units.en: Wang Shizhen also greatly esteemed Jiru, and celebrated gentlemen of the Three Wu all vied to have him as teacher or friend.
units.literal: Wang Shizhen also greatly esteemed Jiru, and celebrated gentlemen of the Three Wu all vied to have him as teacher or friend.

units.zh: 繼儒通明高邁，年甫二十九，取儒衣冠焚棄之。
units.en: Jiru was clear-sighted and lofty in spirit. At only twenty-nine he took his Confucian cap and robes and burned them.
units.literal: Jiru was clear-sighted and lofty; at only twenty-nine he took his Confucian cap and robes and burned them.

units.zh: 隱居昆山之陽，構廟祀二陸，草堂數椽，焚香晏坐，意豁如也。
units.en: He lived in seclusion on the south slope of Kunshan, built a shrine to the two Lu brothers, and had a thatched hall of several bays where he burned incense and sat at ease, his mind broad and clear.
units.literal: He lived in seclusion on the south slope of Kunshan, built a shrine to the two Lu, had a thatched hall of several bays, burned incense and sat at ease, his mind broad and clear.

units.zh: 時錫山顧憲成講學東林，招之，謝弗往。
units.en: At the time Gu Xiancheng of Wuxi lectured at the Donglin Academy and invited him, but Jiru declined.
units.literal: At the time Gu Xiancheng of Wuxi lectured at the Donglin Academy and invited him, but he declined and did not go.

units.zh: 親亡，葬神山麓，遂築室東佘山，杜門著述，有終焉之志。
units.en: When his parents died he buried them at the foot of Mount Shen, then built a house on East She Mountain, shut his door to write, and resolved to end his days there.
units.literal: When his parents died he buried them at the foot of Mount Shen, then built a house on East She Mountain, shut his door to write, and had the will to end his days there.

units.zh: 工詩善文，短翰小詞，皆極風致，兼能繪事。
units.en: He was skilled in poetry and prose. His short letters and brief lyrics all reached the utmost elegance, and he could also paint.
units.literal: Skilled in poetry and good at prose, his short letters and brief lyrics all reached the utmost elegance, and he could also paint.

units.zh: 又博文強識，經史諸子、術伎稗官與二氏家言，靡不較核。
units.en: Moreover he was broadly learned and had a powerful memory. The classics and histories, the masters, technical arts, unofficial histories, and the teachings of Buddhism and Daoism—none escaped his careful examination.
units.literal: Moreover he was broadly learned and had a strong memory; the classics and histories, the masters, technical arts, unofficial histories, and the teachings of the two schools—none escaped his careful examination.

units.zh: 或刺取瑣言僻事，詮次成書，遠近競相購寫。
units.en: Sometimes he culled trivial anecdotes and obscure matters, arranged them into books, and readers near and far all vied to purchase and copy them.
units.literal: Sometimes he culled trivial words and obscure matters, arranged them into books, and near and far all vied to purchase and copy them.

units.zh: 征請詩文者無虛日。
units.en: Not a day passed without someone seeking his poetry or prose.
units.literal: Those who sought his poetry and prose had not a vacant day.

units.zh: 性喜獎掖士類，屨常滿戶外，片言酬應，莫不當意去。
units.en: By nature he delighted in encouraging scholars. Visitors' shoes often filled the space outside his door, and with even a brief reply none failed to depart satisfied.
units.literal: By nature he delighted in encouraging scholars; shoes were often full outside his door, and with a word in reply none failed to depart satisfied.

units.zh: 暇則與黃冠老衲窮峰泖之勝，吟嘯忘返，足跡罕入城市。
units.en: In his leisure he joined Daoist priests and old monks to explore the beauties of peaks and the Mao waterways, chanting and whistling until he forgot to return. His footsteps rarely entered the city.
units.literal: In leisure he joined Daoist priests and old monks to exhaust the beauties of peaks and the Mao waterways, chanting and whistling until he forgot to return; his tracks rarely entered the city.

units.zh: 其昌為築來仲樓招之至。
units.en: Qichang built the Laizhong Tower to invite him there.
units.literal: Qichang built the Laizhong Tower to invite him there.

units.zh: 黃道周疏稱「志尚高雅，博學多通，不如繼儒」，其推重如此。
units.en: Huang Daozhou in a memorial praised him as having "lofty and elegant aspirations, broad learning and wide accomplishment—none equal to Jiru." Such was the esteem in which he was held.
units.literal: Huang Daozhou in a memorial praised him as "aspiration lofty and elegant, broadly learned and widely accomplished—none equal to Jiru," so greatly was he esteemed.

units.zh: 侍郎沈演及御史、給事中諸朝貴，先後論薦，謂繼儒道高齒茂，宜如聘吳與弼故事。
units.en: Vice Minister Shen Yan and various eminent officials among censors and supervising secretaries successively recommended him, saying Jiru's Way was lofty and his years advanced, and that he should be invited as Wu Yubi had been.
units.literal: Vice Minister Shen Yan and various eminent officials among censors and supervising secretaries successively recommended him, saying Jiru's Way was lofty and his years advanced, and that he should be invited as in the precedent of Wu Yubi.

units.zh: 屢奉詔征用，皆以疾辭。
units.en: He received repeated imperial summons to office, but each time declined on grounds of illness.
units.literal: Repeatedly he received imperial summons to office, but each time declined on grounds of illness.

units.zh: 卒年八十二，自為遺令，纖悉畢具。
units.en: He died at the age of eighty-two, having drawn up his own final instructions down to the last detail.
units.literal: He died at eighty-two, having himself drawn up his final instructions in every minute detail.
